figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Architectural comparison of unified motion–language modeling paradigms. (a) Language-based motion models discretize motion into tokens and model motion and text within a shared LLM. (b) Continuous motion–language models use the LLM to produce conditioning representations, while motion is generated by an external diffusion module. (c) Möbius brings the denoising process into the unified multimodal backbone, allowing noisy motion and language to interact throughout generation.
figures.headline: Möbius places denoising inside the unified backbone, while prior unified designs run denoising in an external diffusion module.
citing_sentences: Recent unified motion–language models have attempted to unify motion understanding and generation (Zhu et al., 2025; Li et al., 2026; Wang et al., 2026) (see Fig. 2 for an architectural comparison).

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Overview of Möbius. Motion understanding and generation share a unified multimodal backbone. Text tokens, clean motion frames, and noisy target frames with flow time $t$ participate in shared attention at every layer, while role-specific parameters handle normalization, projections, and feed-forward transformations. The text head autoregressively predicts captions, and the motion head recovers target frames in parallel for generation, temporal completion, and editing. The central matrices illustrate attention visibility for motion understanding and generation.
figures.headline: Text, clean motion frames, and noisy target frames attend to each other in shared attention at every layer.
citing_sentences: Möbius unifies motion understanding and generation within a shared representation space (see Figure 3).

abstract: We aim to build a truly unified motion model that can understand, generate, and edit human motion within a single framework. Existing motion UMMs remain only partially unified: motion understanding is handled by a language model, while generation is often delegated to a separate diffusion module operating over learned motion latents. We introduce Möbius, which brings the entire diffusion process into the same multimodal representation space used for motion understanding. Clean motion, noisy motion, and text jointly participate in shared attention, while role-specific parameters process understanding and generation streams. Importantly, Möbius operates directly on continuous frame-level raw motion, requiring neither discrete tokenization nor a pretrained motion VAE. This simple formulation naturally supports motion captioning, text-to-motion generation, temporal completion, and instruction-guided editing within a single model. On HumanML3D, Möbius achieves state-of-the-art performance among unified motion models. Scaling to 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data further demonstrates that our framework is both effective and scalable.

sections.body: The paper asks whether motion understanding and the whole generation process can share one representation space. Möbius places clean motion, noisy motion, and text in shared attention, with separate parameters for each motion role. It operates on continuous frame-level raw motion, without discrete tokenization or a pretrained latent motion model. Training is curriculum-based: understanding is learned first and generation is added afterward. On HumanML3D, the 0.6B model is reported to achieve the best results among unified motion models on generation and captioning. Scaling to 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data gives further gains on the motion-language tasks.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Möbius runs the entire motion diffusion process inside the shared multimodal space used for understanding, not an external module.

sections.body: This section groups prior work into diffusion-based motion generators, discrete-token language models, and unified motion–language models. The unified group includes MotionGPT3, LLaMo, and UniMotion, which use continuous motion representations with language-model backbones. The authors state that these methods still rely on learned motion latent spaces or encoder–decoder interfaces. Möbius instead works on framewise motion features and places denoising inside the unified multimodal backbone. Role-specific projectors and Transformer parameters specialize processing, and noisy motion interacts with motion and language context throughout denoising. Figure 2 contrasts the three designs.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior unified motion models either tokenize motion or hand language features to an external diffusion module.

sections.body: The method represents each clip as frame-level raw motion with 201 values per frame for joint positions and rotations, with no learned motion encoder. Tokens are routed by role: noisy motion uses generation parameters, while text, boundary tokens, and clean motion use understanding parameters. All tokens share one attention operation. Motion tokens attend bidirectionally, and text stays causal. Training has two phases. Phase I initializes from Qwen3 and trains on motion captioning. Phase II initializes the generation parameters from the understanding parameters, freezes the understanding parameters, and trains denoising on a noisy motion built by mixing noise with the target motion. The stated reason is that joint training from the start can disrupt the pretrained language representations.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: Möbius uses raw frame-level motion with role-specific parameters and shared attention, trained understanding-first.

sections.body: Evaluation covers text-to-motion generation and captioning on HumanML3D, instruction-based editing on MotionFix, and temporal completion, plus ablations. In Table 1, Möbius-0.6B reports R@1 of 0.8209 and FID of 6.1291, against 0.6709 and 20.9913 for MotionGPT3, the strongest unified baseline in that table. The 1.7B variant has lower R@1 (0.7968) but lower FID (10.6642). In Table 2, captioning BLEU-4 is 0.2032 for the 0.6B model versus 0.1605 for MotionGPT3. In Table 3, the editing variant trained with MotionFix pairs reaches FID 0.0955 versus 0.1339 for MotionLab. The ablations in Table 4 favor role-separated parameters and understanding-first training.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Möbius-0.6B scores 0.8209 on top-1 retrieval and 6.1291 on Fréchet distance, ahead of unified baselines.

sections.body: The conclusion restates that Möbius organizes computation by role rather than modality and supports understanding, generation, editing, and temporal completion in one model. The authors argue that understanding and continuous motion generation need not be linked through a separate latent generator. They cite strong HumanML3D text-to-motion and captioning results and gains at 1.7B parameters and 1,700 hours of motion data. The stated limitation is that experiments cover controlled single-person motion. Future work names multi-person interaction, detailed hand and finger motion, retargeting across body structures, and deployment on real-world robots.
sections.heading: Discussion and Conclusion
sections.headline: The authors conclude the shared space works at 1.7B scale, with evidence limited to controlled single-person motion.

sections.body:
- Datasets: HumanML3D for the 0.6B model; an internal corpus of about 1,700 hours for the 1.7B model; MotionFix pairs for the editing variant.
- Motion interface: 201-dimensional HY-Motion features at 30 FPS, with normalization details.
- Architecture and training: Table S1 gives total parameters of 1.047B and 3.148B; Table S2 lists hyper-parameters.
- Task construction and inference: Table S3 gives task contexts; Table S4 gives sampler and prompt settings.
- Efficiency: Table S5 reports single-GPU latency and peak memory.
- Evaluation: protocols for HumanML3D generation, captioning, editing, and completion, plus extra completion metrics.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists datasets, architecture and training settings, task construction, inference settings, timing, evaluation protocols, and extra completion results.
